title: add-causal-traffic-attribution-canary-with-adaptive-throttle-fence
author: Arjun Patel
description:
Context & motivation:
We observed intermittent throughput regressions during canary rollouts where traffic shape shifts (short bursts from mobile clients) amplified tail latency and confounded our baseline detectors. Current canary signal fusion treats slices independently and produces noisy attributions, resulting in unnecessary rollbacks or over-conservative throttles.

This PR introduces a causal attribution layer for the perf-canary pipeline and pairs it with an adaptive throttle fence that enforces traffic-aware soft throttles during uncertain attributions. The goal is to reduce false-positive rollbacks while maintaining SLO protection for high-risk cohorts.

What this changes (high-level):
- New component: causal_attributor service that uses lightweight counterfactual shadowing + propensity scoring to estimate whether observed degradation is attributable to the candidate model or to traffic covariates.
- Adaptive throttle fence: a pluggable rollout guard that applies transient, cohort-weighted throttles when attribution confidence is low and risk to SLOs is high. Throttles decay automatically once attribution confidence improves.
- Probe prioritizer: schedules synthetic probes into under-represented cohorts to improve attribution confidence faster.
- Metric augmentation: adds per-cohort traffic features (median payload size, client-type, concurrency bucket) to the canary feature set used by detectors.
- Telemetry & runbooks: new dashboards, traces and an on-call guide for interpreting attribution scores and throttle events.

Why this is different:
Instead of only thresholding metric deltas, the attributor estimates a counterfactual by shadowing a small fraction of production traffic (shadow traffic is forked and routed to the candidate model without impacting the real response path) and measuring divergence conditioned on covariates. The system then uses inverse-propensity weighting to reduce confounding from traffic shifts. The throttle fence is conservative: it starts as a soft traffic cap (reduce candidate share for specific cohorts) and falls back to full rollback only if the attribution and direct perf signals both indicate regression.

Small illustrative snippet (core heuristic used):
"""python
# inverse-propensity weighted divergence estimator (simplified)
weight = 1.0 / max(propensity(candidate), 1e-6)
divergence = weight * kl_divergence(prod_distribution, candidate_distribution)
confidence = 1.0 - sigmoid( a * divergence + b * covariate_variance )
# low confidence -> trigger soft throttle for affected cohorts
"""

Testing & CI notes:
- Local integration harness used to replay production slices and synthetic spikes; added new e2e scenario that reproduces a mobile-burst tail event.
- CI initially failed on a flaky probe scheduler test (test_probe_backoff) — root cause: race in the test harness; fixed by adding deterministic clock injection.
- All unit and integration checks now pass in CI.

Rollout plan:
1) Feature flag default=off; enable for internal canaries only (team: perf-canary)
2) Stage to 5% of rollouts for 48h with verbose debugging enabled
3) Close-loop: if throttle fence events >3 in 24h for same cohort, auto-disable and page oncall for investigation
4) After stability window (2 weeks) progressively increase to 25% then global enable for non-critical releases

Runbook excerpt (how to interpret events):
- Attribution score near 0.8+ AND throughput delta > 5% -> likely candidate regression; consider rollback if SLOs at risk.
- Attribution low (<0.4) and covariate variance high -> suspect traffic shift; throttle fence will reduce candidate share for high-variance cohorts while probes collect more signal.
- Throttle fence log example: "fence: cohort=mobile-102, action=soft-cap, new_share=0.12, decay=15m, reason=low-confidence-high-variance"

Related work & references:
- ENG-3421: background on cohort-based detectors
- ENG-3499: earlier experiment with shadowing for rerankers

Notes for reviewers:
- The attributor includes approximations (IPW and lightweight shadowing) to keep CPU/GPU overhead low; we intentionally avoided heavy causal inference libraries to minimize ops burden.
- Config knobs are intentionally conservative; we expect tuning after a canary window.
- Security: shadowing forks only headers+payload to candidate and respects PII redaction pipeline; included a KMS-backed toggle for further access control.

Merge outcome:
- Approved by reviewers Maya Chen and Diego Alvarez after two rounds of feedback.
- Requested change: make throttle decay configurable per-cohort (addressed in commit 9b1f0ab).
- CI green on final build; merged via squash to main on 2026-02-18.

Release notes:
- New canary capability: causal attribution + adaptive throttle fence for cohort-aware rollouts. Reduces false-positive rollbacks during traffic shifts and adds safer soft throttling behavior.
